text: Untitled #96 is a color photograph created by American visual artist Cindy Sherman in 1981 and is part of her Centerfold series, which consists of 12 images. The photograph shows Sherman portraying a young teenage girl with short blonde hair lying on a linoleum floor, wearing an orange sweater and a short skirt, holding a scrap of newspaper. Sherman described the scene as depicting a young girl who may have been cleaning the kitchen for her mother and tore out a piece of the newspaper containing questions such as "Are you lonely?" or "Do you want to be friends?" or "Do you want to go on a vacation?" while thinking about them. On 11 May 2011, a print of the photograph was auctioned for US$3.89 million, setting a record as the highest price ever paid for a photographic print at that time, although this price has since been exceeded. Another print was sold for $2,882,500 at Christie's New York on 8 May 2012. Prints of the photograph are held in the collections of the Museum of Modern Art in New York, The Art Institute of Chicago, and the Museum Boijmans van Beuningen in Rotterdam.
